item.title: Profits of China's major industrial firms up 15.7 pct in first eight months
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 -- Profits of China's industrial firms above designated size increased 15.7 percent year on year during the first eight months of 2026, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Monday. These industrial firms with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.97 million U.S. dollars) saw their combined profits reach 5.27 trillion yuan in the January-August period, according to the data.

item.title: China's green development momentum keeps growing: ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 27 -- China's green development momentum is growing steadily amid the country's accelerated transformation, Minister of Ecology and Environment Huang Runqiu said here on Sunday. He made the remarks at the opening ceremony of the 2026 annual general meeting of the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development (CCICED). As a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation is accelerating and making breakthroughs, digital and intelligent technologies are deeply integrated with green development, creating new opportunities for addressing global challenges, he said. The international community has voiced louder calls and stronger aspirations for solidarity, cooperation and green development, Huang noted. China unswervingly follows the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and green development, advances carbon reduction, pollution reduction, green expansion and economic growth in a coordinated way, and continuously reinforces the green foundation of high-quality development, he said. China promotes global green and environmental cooperation through its own actions and has always been a steadfast doer and important contributor to global green development, he said. To date, China has built the world's largest clean electricity generation system and steel production system. Renewable energy installed capacity accounts for more than 60 percent of the country's total installed capacity, and nearly four in every 10 kilowatt-hours of electricity consumed by the whole society are green power. In 2025, China's production and sales of new energy vehicles both exceeded 16 million units, ranking first in the world for the 11th consecutive year. Green and low-carbon industries have become a new engine of economic growth. In the first half of this year, coal-fired power generation accounted for less than 50 percent of total electricity generation for the first time. Founded in 1992, the CCICED is a high-level policy advisory body and two-way exchange platform in the field of environment and development. This year's annual general meeting is themed "Pragmatic and Innovative Cooperation, Advancing Together for Green Development."

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to high-level dialogue marking 5th anniversary of GDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) held at the UN headquarters in New York on Friday. Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind, Xi said. Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted. Xi pointed out that nowadays, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and people in all countries are more keen about development. As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said.

item.title: China and the United States reach eight deliverables and understandings
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
WASHINGTON, Sept. 26 -- From Sept. 23 to 25 local time, Chinese President Xi Jinping paid a state visit to the United States. During the visit, the two heads of state had in-depth discussions on the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and major international and regional issues, and reached eight deliverables and understandings: 1. The two sides agree to build "a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity." 2. China and the United States support each other in successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit. The two heads of state intend to attend each other's meetings. 3. The two heads of state agree that Iran should honor its commitment to not developing nuclear weapons, and no country or institution can be allowed to impose tolls on international waterways. 4. The two heads of state recall that China and the U.S. were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war. 5. The two heads of state recognize the positive role of the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, endorse the outcomes of the consultations between the two economic and trade teams, including establishing and taking forward the Board of Trade and other mechanisms, reaching an arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S.-dollar reciprocal tariff reduction, and the extension of the outcomes of economic and trade consultations in Kuala Lumpur, and give instructions that they be implemented. 6. The two sides note that cooperation between the counter-narcotics and law enforcement agencies of China and the U.S. has produced visible outcomes. Recently, the two sides working closely together have jointly cracked multiple cases involving New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) and precursor chemicals, and apprehended dozens of relevant criminal suspects in the two countries. 7. The two sides agree on the establishment of the China-U.S. AI Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI. The next exchange will occur in November 2026. China and the U.S. also agree to establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents. 8. The United States welcomes the arrival of two giant pandas, leased by China to Zoo Atlanta. In addition, the Chinese and U.S. militaries agree to conclude a memorandum of understanding on crisis communication and prevention as soon as possible, and continue their cooperation to search for the remains of missing U.S. servicemembers in China.

item.title: China issues revised regulations on implementation of audit law
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the implementation of the audit law. The revised regulations, which consist of 7 chapters and 64 articles, will take effect on Dec. 1. Highlighting the need to refine and improve audit supervision, the regulations specify the scope and content of audits over fiscal revenues and expenditures, and bring the management and use of state-owned resources into the scope of special audit investigations, among others. To ensure that audit work is free from interference, the regulations add provisions on a registration and reporting system for any unwarranted attempts to inquire about or interfere with audit matters. All departments of the State Council and local authorities at all levels shall strengthen overall coordination, oversee rectification of problems uncovered in audits, and establish and improve relevant systems.

item.title: China to ease market access, boost digital trade: Premier Li
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
HANGZHOU, Sept. 24 -- China will further ease market access and improve policies for cross-border e-commerce retail imports, Premier Li Qiang said Thursday, pledging to share opportunities in its market with other countries. Addressing the opening ceremony of the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Li said the rapid growth of digital trade had created new opportunities, but had also brought widening development gaps, new trade barriers and gaps in international rules into sharper focus. Li called for closer international cooperation to strengthen digital connectivity and advance the alignment and mutual recognition of standards. The international community should enhance North-South cooperation in the field of digital trade, and provide more support to developing countries in terms of technology, infrastructure and personnel training, he said. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, and Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, Adylbek Aleshovich Kasymaliev, also addressed the opening ceremony, which was attended by more than 1,200 representatives from nearly 50 countries and regions, as well as international organizations. The expo, an event dedicated to promoting digital trade and industrial cooperation, is running until Sept. 27, with artificial intelligence as its main theme. China's digital trade has expanded rapidly in recent years. The country's digitally deliverable service trade value expanded at an average annual rate of 11.2 percent between 2016 and 2025, outpacing the global average by 1.8 percentage points.
